makingOf.title: How Saqi is built
makingOf.intro: Five short scenes: the design system, the water maths, the explanations, the tests, and who made it.

scene1.title: One file decides how it looks.
scene1.body: Every colour, size and motion in Saqi comes from design.md. It is checked against the Stylebase schema and compiled into tokens, so the water scale on the map is these seven lines.
scene1.caption: design.md · the colour block (excerpt)

scene2.title: Water first.
scene2.body: A block is watered only when tomorrow’s crop use would take it below its threshold, and only back up to its target. This is the whole sum for D-1, Khalas palms, with ET₀ at 5.8 mm.
scene2.note: The engine never rounds inside; figures round only when shown.

scene3.title: Every decision explains itself.
scene3.body: No black box. Each recommendation carries the reasons that produced it, in the order the engine checked them. These three come straight from the engine.

scene4.title: Tested like production.
scene4.body: The engine is pure functions under table-driven tests. The API and the web app have their own suites, and every change has to pass all of them.

scene5.title: Built by Husni Ramdani.
scene5.body: Built for a farm that doesn’t exist yet, to show how I’d build for one that does.

hero.disclosure:
Farm 07 · Al Ain (fictional)
24.21 N · 55.74 E · GST
hero.title: Water what the soil asks for.
hero.thesis: Tonight’s irrigation, decided by 21:30 GST — with the reasons.
hero.body: Saqi reads live evapotranspiration and soil moisture at two depths, then plans which blocks to water tonight, how many cubic metres, and in what order.
hero.foot: What’s below the surface matters more.

status.label: Data status
status.live: Weather and ET₀ live from Open-Meteo

about.ringLabel: D-1 plant-available water 68 percent, threshold 65, target 90
about.statement: Saqi — Arabic for the one who waters — turns weather and soil readings into a plan a farm manager can trust or override. No fixed schedules, no habit: every block gets a decision, a volume and the reasons behind both.
about.et0Label: Sample reference evapotranspiration over the next seven days, between 5.7 and 6.3 millimetres; 5.8 tomorrow

why.title: Water is the binding constraint.

imports.text: of the UAE’s food is imported today.

target.text: local production is the national target for 2051.

holding.text: Skipping a night while palms still hold this much plant-available water saves water without losing yield (ICARDA).

why.quote: At 21:30, tell me which blocks to water tonight, how many cubic metres, in what order — and show me why, so I can trust it or override it.
why.soilLabel: Soil cross-section of block D-1: root zone 600 millimetres; sensor at 30 centimetres reads 70.4 percent, at 60 centimetres 64.4 percent; block water 68 percent against a 65 percent threshold

product.title: Four surfaces, one decision.
product.lead: The farm manager plans in the evening on a laptop or phone. The crew works the blocks in the morning. Both see the same plan, in their own language.

today.title: Today
today.body: The farm map, tonight’s schedule, the month’s water budget and what needs attention — on one screen.

block.title: Block detail
block.body: Fourteen days of plant-available water, the threshold, every irrigation — and why tonight’s volume is what it is.

field.title: Field companion
field.body: Tasks grouped by block, 56 px buttons, an offline outbox — in English, Arabic and Urdu.

making.title: Making-of
making.body: A scroll story of the water model, the design tokens and the tests behind every number.

farm.title: Seven blocks. One pump. One night window.
farm.lead: Drawn from the farm layout: palms on recycled water, greenhouses on RO, fodder on the outer block. Colour is plant-available water — darker is wetter; the orange lines carry tonight’s water.
farm.mapSummary: Map of {farm}. Watered tonight: {irrigated}. The complete table is available in the List view.
farm.note: D-1 runs first, F-1 follows at 01:01 GST — together they would exceed the 60 m³/h pump. The other five skip or pulse tomorrow.

legend.water: Plant-available water scale, dry to wet

decision.title: Every decision explains itself.
decision.lead: A pure engine: no network, no clock, no randomness — the same inputs always give the same plan. Pick a decision to read the reasoning behind it.

irrigate.summary: Refill from tomorrow’s projected water to the 90% target.

skip.summary: Above threshold after tomorrow’s crop use; saves {saved} m³.

deficit.summary: Runs at 70% because the monthly water budget is tight.

pulse.summary: Three short greenhouse pulses replace tomorrow’s crop use.

instruments.title: Small instruments, honest numbers.
instruments.lead: Every figure carries its unit, its source and its age. Nothing on screen is decoration — if it moves, water moved.
instruments.pulseLabel: Greenhouse pulses tomorrow at 07:00, 11:00 and 15:00 GST
instruments.sensorLabel: D-3 sample sensor readings: the 30 centimetre sensor reports continuously; the 60 centimetre sensor has been offline since 12:00 GST
instruments.savedLabel: Saved: D-2 25, D-3 23, D-4 14 cubic metres
instruments.footnote: Figures are the engine’s worked example for fictional Farm 07 (ET₀ tomorrow 5.8 mm). In the cockpit, weather and ET₀ are fetched live from Open-Meteo and every soil reading is simulated.

field.title: Built for bright sun, gloves and patchy signal.

targets.label: 56 px
targets.body: Every action is a big, high-contrast target — readable at noon, pressable with work gloves.

outbox.label: Outbox
outbox.body: No signal at the far block? “Mark done” queues on the phone and syncs when the connection returns.

languages.label: EN · ع · ار
languages.body: English, Arabic and Urdu. The whole layout mirrors right-to-left; numbers stay Western.

field.phoneDescription: Two inert phone illustrations show the same Field tasks in English and Arabic, including offline saved changes.

making.title: How it was built, in three chapters.
making.lead: The making-of page tells the engineering story behind the plan — for anyone who wants to check the working.

tokens.title: One file decides how it looks.
tokens.body: Colour, type, spacing and motion live in a single design file and are generated into tokens. Nothing on screen is picked by hand twice.

water.title: Water first.
water.body: The water-balance model, built term by term with D-1’s numbers: from 68.0% today to 90.4 m³ tonight.

tests.title: Tested like production.
tests.body: A pure engine under table-driven tests, Playwright journeys across the product, and CI on every commit.
